guide.summary: Written evidence explains your inquiry and process to readers who see only images and short text. This unit covers concise statements, documenting and photographing work, and originality and ethical use of references and tools.

sections.heading: Writing concisely
sections.body: Portfolio writing is short and specific. Use concrete nouns and verbs: name materials (vine charcoal, gouache, cyanotype), processes (scraping, layering, collaging, editing in layers), and decisions (cropped tighter, reduced palette). Avoid filler such as 'I explored many things' or 'I expressed my feelings'. Each sentence should help a reader understand your questions, process, or choices.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Photograph work in even, indirect light, square to the camera, with accurate color and clean cropping. Include details that show technique and process images that show development. Keep a log of dates, materials, and decisions so your written responses are accurate.

sections.heading: Originality and references
sections.body: Your work must be your own. If you use reference photos or other sources, transform them significantly through your own choices, and be ready to show how. A new AI policy applies in 2026-27: read the current AP Art and Design guidelines before using any AI tools, and follow your teacher's instructions. Being transparent about your process protects the integrity of your portfolio.

keyTakeaways: Photograph accurately; include details and process.
Transform references; follow the AI policy.
commonMistakes: Using others' images without significant transformation.
examTips: Read statements aloud to cut filler.
Check the current AP policies each year.
guide.cramSheet:
**Writing:** concrete · specific · concise · materials, processes, decisions

**Photos:** even light · square · true color · clean crop · details · process

**Integrity:** your own work · transform references · current AI policy · process log

vocab.definition: Written explanation of an artist's work and intent.
Brief listing of ideas, materials, and processes.
Record of dates, materials, and decisions.
Significant change to a source through one's own choices.
Using existing images in new work.
Honesty and originality in one's work.
Description of how and why work changed.

practice.stem: Why include detail images in a portfolio?

choices.text: To show technique and surface qualities a full view can't reveal
To increase the number of finished works

practice.prompt: Rewrite this identification to be specific: 'Ideas: feelings. Materials: mixed media. Processes: art.'
practice.sampleResponse: Ideas: layered memory of a demolished block. Materials: archival photos, inkjet prints, acrylic, tape. Processes: scanning, cutting, layering, glazing.

practice.prompt: Describe your plan for photographing and documenting your work across the year.

rubric.description: Plan for process and detail images.

practice.sampleResponse: I'll photograph each finished piece near a north-facing window on an overcast day, camera on a tripod square to the work, and check color against the original. Every week I'll photograph sketches and in-progress stages and record dates, materials, and decisions in a process log. For each major piece I'll capture two details that show technique.

practice.prompt: Explain how you will use reference material (photos, artworks, or digital tools) responsibly in your portfolio.

rubric.description: Commits to originality and significant transformation.
Mentions following current AP policies, including AI.

practice.sampleResponse: I'll take my own reference photographs whenever possible. When I use another source, I'll combine it with my own images and change composition, scale, and medium so the final work reflects my choices. I'll keep references in my process log to show the transformation, and I'll check the current AP Art and Design AI policy with my teacher before using any digital tool.

practice.prompt: Write a short revision statement describing feedback you received on a piece and how you changed the work.

rubric.description: Explains why changes improved the work.

practice.sampleResponse: Classmates said the figure blended into the background. I darkened the background values, simplified the edges around the figure, and added a warm accent at the face. The figure now reads first, which strengthens the sense of isolation the piece is about.
